hook.text: In a leveraged buyout, the buyer uses the target company's own future profits to pay off the debt used to buy it.

buildup.text: Private equity firms specialize in LBOs. They put up 30% equity and borrow 70%.

discovery.text: If the company grows, the equity investors make enormous returns because leverage amplifies gains.

twist.text: When earnings wobble, the debt that boosted returns becomes a vise on jobs, investment, and survival.

climax.text: LBOs are financial engineering. They bet that future profits will cover today's debt. When the bet fails, companies die.

punchline.text: Buy with borrowed money, repay with profits. LBOs are leveraged bets.

quiz.question: What destroyed Toys R Us despite $11 billion in revenue?
options: $5 billion in debt from its leveraged buyout
